Plot a variation array

Source: R/coda_diagnostics.r
plot.ecodive_variation_array.Rd

Draws a variation_array() as two heatmaps on one grid: the variances of the log ratios above the diagonal, their means below, and beside each row the feature's share of the total variance.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ecodive_variation_array'
plot(x, digits = 2L, key = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

x

A variation array, from variation_array().

digits

The number of decimal places of the values written in the cells, when there are at most 15 features. Default 2.

key

Whether to draw the two colour keys on the right. Default TRUE.

...

Passed on to graphics::image(), such as main, sub, or useRaster.

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

The features run from the first at the top to the last at the bottom, and from left to right in the same order. Their order is the one x was made with (its clust), or else average-linkage clustering of the distances \(\sqrt{\tau_{ij}}\), so that nearly proportional features sit together. x itself isn't changed.

Cells above the diagonal are coloured by \(\tau_{ij}\), from light (proportional) to dark red; cells below by the mean log ratio of the row's feature over the column's, blue for negative and red for positive, symmetric about 0. The bars on the right are each feature's clr variance as a percentage of the total variance ("% clr var", as in Pawlowsky-Glahn & Egozcue 2011).

See also

variation_array(), plot.ecodive_dist() for vlr() alone.

Examples

    x <- replace_zeros(ex_counts, 'mult')
    plot(variation_array(x))
